newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bel-20 ends above 1,900 for the first time.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bel-20 ends above 1,900 for the first time.

text.p: Dollar and Belgian bond strength on Wednesday helped Belgian shares shrug off a slightly weaker performance on Wall Street in the afternoon and lifted the Bel-20 leading share index further into record territory.
The Bel-20 index finished 12.88 points or 0.68 percent higher at 1,904.82, a new closing high, after peaking intra-day at 1,911.58. The last records were set two days ago.

"We saw a big buy order going through in selected blue chip stocks including Solvay, Petrofina and Electrabel. It had all the characteristics of a foreign investor who wanted to make up a portfolio of Belgian stocks," one dealer said.
Petrofina climbed 1.9 percent or 200 francs to 10,725, Solvay rose 225 francs - both in solid volume - and Electrabel gained 30 francs to 7,500.

"I'm rather positive for the next few weeks - there will be signs of economic slow down and (market) rates will come down," the dealer added. This would lead to a switch out of cyclicals and into more defensive stocks.

Meanwhile attention for the rest of this week will focus on Germany and the United States, with a Bundesbank meeting and U.S. producer price and weekly jobless claims data due on Thursday, followed by monthly jobless figures on Friday.

Retailer Colruyt, which gained 50 francs to 14,000, announced after the market closed that consolidated net profit rose 11.6 percent in the first half of its 1996/1997 financial year, more or less in line with expectations.
The company forecast a full year net profit of at least 2.15 billion francs compared to 1.934 the previous year.

Steel maker Cockerill Sambre shed 9.0 percent to 121 francs, partly in a technical correction after recent gains and partly on a gloomy outlook for 1997 it gave during an analysts' meeting on Tuesday.
